title: Sessionized slabbed pricing scratchpad
content:
Quick brain dump: sessionized + slabbed pricing idea (very rough)

Context / motivation
- Want something between pure PAYG per-token and big reserved commitments that:
  * reduces friction for interactive apps (chat agents) where user sessions have many tiny requests
  * gives predictable revenue / SLO-backed buckets for customers who need a floor but not big commits
  * credits caching and KV reuse implicitly (sessions reuse prefix/state so unit cost lower)

High-level concept
- Sell bundles of session-units rather than flat tokens. Each session-unit = a short-lived conversation allocation (e.g., 1 session-unit = up to 5k generated tokens + 25k input tokens OR 30s of steady interaction).
- Implement slabbed consumption inside each session-unit: smaller sessions consume a fraction of a unit (e.g., 0.2 units), long sessions consume multiple units. Pricing does not charge per token directly for sessions inside unit boundaries; instead we price unit at an amortized GPU-hour/token-equivalent.
- Provide a PAYG token price for anything beyond units and a burst top-up mechanism.

Back-of-envelope numbers (assumptions)
- Baseline model: 70B decoder-ish (quantized), production optimized, sustained throughput mapping: 1 A100-80GB GPU ~= 3M tokens/hour of generated tokens at typical avg seq lengths and batching. (placeholder; validate with infra).
- Effective token per GPU‑hour: conservatively 2.5M gen tokens/hour after overheads, KV memory, small requests.
- Want unit price to roughly equal cost + 40% margin for hosted starter plans. If infra cost per GPU-hour = $3 (example committed price), then cost per token = $3 / 2.5M = $0.0000012 per token (gen). Add other infra (storage, network, control plane) ~+25% => ~$0.0000015/token. With margin, target price = $0.0000021/token.

Define session-unit mapping (first pass)
- 1 session-unit = 5k generated tokens amortized + 25k input tokens (because input is cheaper but still non-zero)
- Equivalent token count for pricing = generated_tokens + 0.2 * input_tokens => mapped tokens per unit = 5k + 0.2*25k = 10k mapped-tokens
- Using target price $0.0000021/token => unit price = 10k * 0.0000021 = $0.021 per session-unit.

Use-cases / perceived value
- Chatbots used in-product with many short exchanges (50–200 tokens generated each call): without session units, customer sees many tiny token charges and high variance; session units smooth spend.
- Mobile assistants with high latency sensitivity: we can offer a slight premium for SLO-backed session routing (edge GPUs).
- Customer psychological pricing: ‘200 sessions for $4.20/mo’ is easier to round and forecast than raw token counts.

Slabbed consumption rules (sketch)
- On session start, allocate one provisional unit and start a short TTL (e.g., 10 minutes).
- Track session mapped-tokens (gen + 0.2*input).
- Consumption slab table: 0–2k mapped-tokens => 0.25 units; 2k–6k => 1 unit; 6k–12k => 2 units; >12k => pay PAYG per token for excess + additional whole units allocated per multiple of 10k.
- Rationale: reward small interactions (0.25 units) and avoid cliff effects for moderate sessions. 

Burst/top-up model
- Customers can enable session-bursting: allow sessions to temporarily exceed committed units and bill at a burst price (e.g., 1.6x unit price) until account is rebalanced. Useful for product launches.

FAQ / open questions (TODO)
- How to handle streaming partial results (long-running streaming sessions)? Map by throughput/time vs token count? Maybe time-based slab for streaming-only flows.
- Accounting complexity in invoices: need clear line items: units consumed, PAYG overage tokens, burst charges.
- How to credit cache/KV reuse across sessions for same user? If prefix cached on our side reduces effective cost, should that be explicit discount or implicit expected in unit sizing?
- Edge routing SLO premium: how to price? Per session-unit premium vs per-call latency surcharge?
- Fraud/abuse surface: session units might be used to batch small requests. Need rate-limits per-account and per-user to avoid gaming.

Quick sample tiers (starter idea)
- Micro: 500 session-units / month -> $9.99/mo (~$0.01998/unit) targeted at indie apps.
- Starter: 3k units / month -> $49/mo (~$0.0163/unit) volume discount, includes 99th percentile latency SLO (region-only).
- Scale: 50k units / month -> $699/mo (~$0.01398/unit) plus dedicated routing guarantees and 24h support.
- Dedicated/Enterprise: custom, reserved GPU pools tie to units (units per reserved GPU-hour mapping) and committed overage discount.

Simple math examples for product manager slides
- User A: lightweight bot, average session 600 gen tokens -> mapped 600 + 0.2*2400(input)=600+480=1080 mapped -> 1080/10k = 0.108 units -> billed 0.25 units (slab) = $0.00525 per session. If user does 100 sessions/day => 25 units/day -> 750 units/mo -> ~$15.75/mo.
- User B: heavy worker, average session 20k gen tokens -> mapped ~20k + 0.2*5k=21k -> 2.1 units -> billed as 2 units + PAYG 0.1*10k mapped -> complexity but net >2 units. Consider explicit large-session plan.

Implementation notes (tech debt / infra hooks)
- Need session-id propagation through API -> server allocates a provisional unit with short TTL and returns unit allocation metadata.
- Metering pipeline needs per-session aggregated counters and slabbing logic downstream (not per-request tokens only).
- Billing exporter needs to emit both unit-events and raw-token-events for audits.
- Console: show sessions left, average mapped tokens per session, and projected burn rate.

Next steps (for me)
- Validate GPU-hour -> tokens number with infra (ping @Miguel) and get quantized throughput for our 70B / 13B variants.
- Run a 1-week sample: instrument internal app that generates 5k sessions/day and report mapped-token distribution.
- Propose a simple pricing table to PM and Growth for A/B test (pricing UI experiment).

Notes to self: keep this simple for MVP. The client-facing UX should avoid complicated formulas; surface "sessions" and credits left. Technical teams can see the detailed mapping under the hood.

End of scratchpad.
